draft.title: Sedimentary rocks
card: Sediments are loose pieces of rock, sand, mud or shell, or the remains of living things. Water, wind or ice carry them and drop them in a new place.
Sediments settle in layers, with the oldest usually at the bottom. Over a very long time, newer layers bury the older ones, and their weight squeezes the grains together.

Cementing is a separate step: minerals in the water glue the grains together. This turns buried sediment into sedimentary rock, such as sandstone. Limestone is another, made mostly from shells and the remains of sea life.
Most fossils are found in sedimentary rock, and limestone often holds them. A dead animal buried in soft sediment can be kept as the sediment becomes rock.
draft.remember: Sedimentary rock is made from layers of sediment that are buried and cemented over a long time.

opts: Sand is laid down, buried and cemented into rock
Sand is melted deep underground, then cools into rock
Sand is changed by heat and pressure without melting
Sand is blown into a pile and stays as loose grains
a.why: Sandstone is sedimentary, so it forms when sand is laid down in layers, buried and cemented. Melting is not part of how sedimentary rock forms, and a loose pile of sand has not been buried or cemented, so it is not rock.
a.clue: Think about layers, burial and glue-like minerals.

b.q: Mud settles in layers on the floor of a lake in Victoria. A dead fish is buried in one layer. Over millions of years the layers harden. Where is the fish fossil most likely to be found?
opts: In sedimentary rock formed from the mud
In igneous rock formed from cooled lava
In the loose mud at the surface today
In rock that was melted and then cooled
b.why: The mud was buried in layers and cemented, so it became sedimentary rock, which is where most fossils are found. The fish was buried in mud, not lava, so igneous rock formed from cooled lava is not where it would be kept.
b.clue: What kind of rock does buried, hardened mud become?

a.best: Sand is laid down, buried and cemented into rock

b.best: In sedimentary rock formed from the mud
